title: Newsom Reappoints Two Indian-Origin Dentists to California Dental Boards
excerpt: Ram Vaderhobli of Belmont continues on the Dental Board of California and Sridevi Ponnala of Fremont on the Dental Hygiene Board, in Governor Newsom's October 14 appointments round; both trained first in India and neither seat requires Senate confirmation.
body:
• Governor Gavin Newsom has reappointed Ram Vaderhobli of Belmont to the Dental Board of California, where he has served since 2025.
  • Sridevi Ponnala of Fremont has been reappointed to the Dental Hygiene Board of California, where she has served since 2023.
  • Both trained first in India — Vaderhobli at R.V. Dental College and Ponnala at M.R. Ambedkar Dental College — before building careers in California dentistry.
  • Neither position requires Senate confirmation; each pays $100 per diem, according to the Governor's October 14 announcement.

California Governor Gavin Newsom has reappointed two Indian-origin dental professionals to the state boards that oversee dentistry and dental hygiene, according to an announcement from the Governor's office on October 14. Ram Vaderhobli of Belmont will continue on the Dental Board of California, and Sridevi Ponnala of Fremont will continue on the Dental Hygiene Board of California. Both were first trained as dentists in India and now hold senior roles in California's dental education and community health systems.

Ram Vaderhobli, Dental Board of California

Vaderhobli has served on the Dental Board of California since 2025. He has been a Clinical Professor of Preventive and Restorative Dental Sciences at the University of California, San Francisco School of Dentistry since 2020, and Dental Director for its Advanced Education in General Dentistry programme since 2010. He has held positions at the UCSF School of Dentistry since 2007, including Health Sciences Assistant Clinical Professor, Health Sciences Associate Clinical Professor, and Clinical Director for Computer-Aided Design and Computer-Aided Manufacturing.

Before and alongside his UCSF work, Vaderhobli was California Regional Assistant Director for the Advanced Education in General Dentistry Program at Lutheran Medical Center from 2011 to 2015, and a resident in the same programme at the Eastman Institute for Oral Health of the University of Rochester from 2005 to 2006. He held positions at the American Dental Association Paffenbarger Research Center from 2003 to 2004, including Research Specialist and Guest Scientist, and was a Research Assistant at Alfred University from 2002 to 2003. He is a Fellow of the American College of Dentists, the International College of Dentists and the Pierre Fauchard Academy, and a member of bodies including the American Dental Education Association and the Indian Dental Association. He earned a Master of Science degree in Biomaterials Engineering from Alfred University and a Bachelor of Dental Surgery degree from R.V. Dental College in India. He is registered without party preference.

Sridevi Ponnala, Dental Hygiene Board of California

Ponnala has served on the Dental Hygiene Board of California since 2023. She has been Chief Integration Officer at Tiburcio Vasquez Health Center since 2021, where she has held multiple positions since 2010, including Chief Dental Officer and Dental Director. She was an Adjunct Faculty member in the Chabot Hygiene Program at the Chabot-Las Positas Community College District from 2016 to 2019, and Clinical Director at the Native American Health Center from 2007 to 2010.

Her training spans both countries: a Doctor of Dental Surgery degree from the University of California, San Francisco School of Dentistry, a Master of Business Administration degree from California State University, East Bay, and a Bachelor of Dental Surgery degree from M.R. Ambedkar Dental College in India. She is a Democrat.

The wider appointments round

The two reappointments were part of a larger October 14 appointments announcement. In the same round, Kevin Cheng of San Marino was reappointed to the Dental Board of California, where he has served since 2024, Cara Miyasaki of San Jose was appointed to the Dental Board, and the Dental Hygiene Board also saw Monika Lee of Sacramento appointed and Sonia "Pat" Hansen of Concord and Naleni Tribble-Agarwal of Newark reappointed. For each of the dental and dental hygiene positions, the Governor's office states that Senate confirmation is not required and compensation is $100 per diem.

The reappointments keep two professionals who trained in India and built careers in California — one in dental education at UCSF, one in community health in the East Bay — on the boards that set standards for the state's dental profession. For the Indian-American dentists and hygienists who practise under those boards, the seats are held by people who took the same route into the profession: a dental degree in India, followed by retraining and licensure in the United States.
